name: flightcrew-core
reason: initial: flightcrew rebuilt as files and native tooling — a launch with its spec series and numbered runs, JSON documents any view can read, a minimal flight command, liftoffs driving a workflow suite, a complete crew, three verdict kinds, enforcement that fails closed, and an ending that is the human's.

intent.text: HITL AI engineering falls short for any large or complex task requiring a human's direct time and attention; an orchestrated agent system can solve this problem. The human front-loads their attention and time into a carefully crafted definition of the work, and beyond that an intelligently built automated system makes the work materialise through agents repeatedly attempting to discover the deterministic outcome. If the agents fail the human simply tries again, bringing the previous failures to improve the definition of the work, the tools used, or the agents' assurance of done. This orchestration toolkit is built for a single Claude Code Max subscription user, leveraging the inbuilt harness and steering infrastructure Claude provides; the product is agent-shaped. If a user's idea of a piece of work can be handed over and agents build it for them, this work has been completed.

scope.text: flightdeck/flightcrew/: the core scripts under bin/, hooks/, crew/ (one file per role), schemas/run/, templates/dispatch/, workflows/, liftoffs/, verify/ (replacing checks/lib, checks/validators and checks/gates), and README.md; the superseded v1 runner, hooks, kickoff library, dispatch templates, schemas directly under schemas/ (other than spec.schema.json) and MANIFEST.txt are deleted.

flightdeck/launch/: README.md, FLIGHTLOG.md, one folder per launch at launch/<name>/ holding launch.json, specs/ and runs/run-<n>/; flightdeck/.controlcenter/ (flightcrew.yaml, launch.yaml) and its .gitignore line; launch/flightcrew-core/ is this work's own launch, and its launch.json, runs/run-1/ and FLIGHTLOG.md exist in that layout before any leaf does.
flightdeck/testbench/: fixtures/, lib/, benches/, and only the suites that cover a leaf, hook, validator, workflow or crew rule this spec names; every other suite is deleted.

flightdeck/manuals/launch/, harness/ and orchestration/ rewritten to the artefacts, roles, workflows, liftoffs and human readings this spec names with no command sequence; manuals/testing/ and library/terms.md aligned to the testing vocabulary; manuals/README.md updated; .claude/workflows/, .claude/agents/, .claude/settings.json and the root CLAUDE.md receive what the install script writes; flightdeck/manuals/operators-manual.md and maintenance-manual.md are written unit by unit.
Out: flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/, flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/, flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/ and flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md are untouched history.

Out: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/spec.schema.json, flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/spec.template.json, flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/spec-builder.md, flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/spec-judge.md, flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/spec-attacker.md, flightdeck/manuals/spec/, flightdeck/manuals/versioning/ and flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/rubrics/ are unchanged in any byte.

Out: a local web view over the run documents, CI configuration, telemetry beyond the events file, any npm package, installing anything beyond what the install script writes into .claude/ and CLAUDE.md, and flightdeck/blackbox/, hangar/, missions/, radar/, library/ (except terms.md), dev/ and the dev-workspace skill.
Out: copying a spec, a tests map or an interview/ folder into a run; rewriting the $id or $schema strings of any schema, template or spec; migrating spec folders on other branches to the new layout.

constraints.text: Node 22 ES modules importing only node: built-ins or relative paths, for every script under flightdeck/flightcrew and flightdeck/testbench; no package.json, node_modules or lock file.

Claude Code agent files: YAML frontmatter using a combination of name, description, tools, model, disallowedTools, permissionMode, isolation, maxTurns and hooks; hooks declared there run only while that agent acts and its Stop hook fires as SubagentStop.

Claude Code hooks: PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SubagentStop can block, by exit 2 or a deny decision; the other events record; the eight-consecutive-block turn ceiling is the built-in stall control, and stderr on exit 0 is shown to nobody.

Claude Code dynamic workflows: a prebuilt JavaScript agent-dispatch and structured-return tool, called by slash command with input args, schema-driven agent returns, custom agent definitions, inbuilt worktrees, model and tier overrides, staged agent progression, parallel concurrency, nested workflows one level deep, repeatable and resumable; no filesystem, shell, clock or randomness.
The Claude Code Bash sandbox: sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite in the installed settings is the only write protection that reaches Bash and its subprocesses.

JSON files with templates and schemas as the mutable data the system inputs and outputs: every run document validates against a schema under flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/, the spec against flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/spec.schema.json.

Check scripts: prebuilt tests returning a verification verdict, one line per case, exiting 0 or 2; a verdict is one of three — an exit code, a ratio against a threshold declared before any trial, or a verdict sheet against a rubric with a quotation on every answer — per flightdeck/manuals/testing/testing-description.md.
Callable scripts: each runs on its own path, prints a single line or its artefact on success, and exits 0 on success, 1 on a usage or environment error, 2 on a failed check or a refused action.

interfaces.name: spec.json
interfaces.text: spec.v<n>.json under flightdeck/launch/<name>/specs/. Schema: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/spec.schema.json. Template: flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/spec.template.json. Communicates: the nine domains, every one present unless a reason is stated; ids immutable after the first freeze; the node change scheme (status ok|new|changed with notes); retired nodes visible across versions; draft or frozen, draft editable and frozen locked by the human's freeze with the commit named; version series for improvable retries.

interfaces.name: launch.json
interfaces.text: launch.json at flightdeck/launch/<name>/. Schema: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/launch.schema.json. Template: flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/launch.template.json. Communicates: name, created, the spec and tests-map versions in force, test_dir (the project's own test folder), current_run, and per run its number, branch 'run/<name>-<n>', base_commit, lock_commit and started. Fields: { schema_version: 1, name: string, created: date, spec: { version: int }, tests_map: { version: int } | null, test_dir: string, current_run: int|null, runs: [ { n: int, branch: string, base_commit: hex, lock_commit: hex|null, started: iso } ] }. The folder around it holds specs/ (spec and map series, interview/) and runs/run-<n>/ (liftoff/, plan.json, plan.md, events.jsonl, hooks.log, checks/ with rubrics/, evidence/, dispatches/, returns/, report.json, report.md).

interfaces.name: tests-map.json
interfaces.text: tests-map.v<n>.json under flightdeck/launch/<name>/specs/. Schema: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/tests-map.schema.json. Template: flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/tests-map.template.json. Communicates: the checks a run is proven by, each with id T<n>, kind, verdict 'exit'|'ratio'|'sheet', covers, command (run from the repository root, {run} expanded to the run folder), depends_on globs, baseline, and for ratio trials and threshold, for sheet a rubric path; locked_paths, quarantined, unverified and retired lists; draft or frozen as I1.

interfaces.name: plan.json
interfaces.text: plan.json at runs/run-<n>/. Schema: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/plan.schema.json. Template: flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/plan.template.json. Communicates: the run's approach, waves (serial or parallel) and units — id, name, kind contracts|feature|integration|proof, spec_refs, checks, owner role, paths, depends_on, scout flag — and risks; frozen as I1 once written; plan.md rendered from it.

interfaces.name: liftoff.json
interfaces.text: A liftoff under flightdeck/flightcrew/liftoffs/<name>.json, copied to runs/run-<n>/liftoff/<name>.json. Schema: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/liftoff.schema.json. Template: flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/liftoff.template.json. Communicates: the recipe a run is conducted by — name, task feature|migration|audit|agent, the sequence of workflows with each one's args, sessions (streams of units per seat, empty for one seat), models per tier, review policy (critic passes, adversary per unit), runtime settings, notes; passed to every workflow as args = { launch, run, liftoff, entry }; named in the log entry as '<name> @ <git log -1 of the library file>'.

interfaces.name: configurations
interfaces.text: Configurations under flightdeck/.controlcenter/, git-ignored: flightcrew.yaml, global system configuration and a placeholder for later global settings; launch.yaml, launch-based configuration holding current_active_launch: <repository-relative launch folder>, written by the init and run-new scripts and editable by hand; every hook and script resolves the run in progress from launch.yaml plus launch.json.current_run, and a worktree reads the main checkout's copy.

interfaces.name: events.jsonl
interfaces.text: events.jsonl at runs/run-<n>/. Schema: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/event.schema.json. Communicates: one object per line — ts, event, launch, run, source hook|leaf|role, session_id, agent_id, agent_type, detail — event being a hook event name or frozen_denied, locked_denied, boundary_denied, log_denied, return, return_invalid, stop_block, check_run, stalled, unit_merged, workflow_end; hooks.log beside it holds '<iso ts> <hook> <message>' lines.

interfaces.name: evidence
interfaces.text: evidence/<T>.json and evidence/summary.json at runs/run-<n>/. Schemas: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/check-result.schema.json (id, command, cwd, exit, verdict, stdout_tail, stderr_tail, duration_ms, ran_at, commit, covers, plus observed { passes, trials } for a ratio and sheet: path for a sheet) and flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/evidence-summary.schema.json = { ran_at: iso, commit: hex, counts: { pass, fail, error, skipped: int }, checks: [ { id, verdict, covers } ], boundary: { base: hex, outside: [string] }, locked: { changed: [string] } }. Communicates: the raw result of every check and the run's verification state.

interfaces.name: report and log
interfaces.text: report.json at runs/run-<n>/ and flightdeck/launch/FLIGHTLOG.md. Schema: flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/run/report.schema.json = { launch, run, header: { spec, kickoff, cost, started, ended }, ledger: [ '[recorded|checked|reviewed|stated] <text>' ], verification: { counts, unverified, quarantined, boundary, locked }, review: { passes, open, resolved }, phases: [ { workflow, ended } ], agents: [ { agent_type, count } ], failures: [ { event, ts, detail } ], notes: string }, rendered to report.md. Template: flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/report.template.md. The log: entries newest first headed '## <YYYY-MM-DD> · <launch> · run-<n>' with lines spec, kickoff, cost, symptom, pr (scribe-written) then outcome, seen on, cause, fixed on, change, watch, kept, reservation, promote (human-owned, '<fill>' until written). Template: flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/runlog-entry.template.md.

behaviours.text: [deterministic] A launch is opened from an idea as one folder holding its spec series and its numbered runs, so that every attempt at one piece of work shares an address and the interval before a spec exists has one too.

[deterministic] A run opens only against a frozen spec and tests map and, after the first, a fully written previous log entry, on its own branch cut from the branch the human is on, so that a retry is a new experiment against an improved setup and never a resumed one.
[deterministic] A frozen document refuses every edit from every tool, the refusal read from the document's own status, so that the freeze holds whether or not any run is in progress.
[deterministic] Every document a run holds validates against its schema at every moment of the run, so that a view layer can read the run's state from the files alone.

[deterministic] The core scripts — init, run-new, freeze, check, render, merge, validate, lint, event, install — each write one artefact inside the launch folder (or under .claude/ and CLAUDE.md for install with --apply), make no network call, and run alone by their own path; no command a human types advances a run.

[statistical] A liftoff pasted into the orchestrator session drives the run through the workflows it names, one per human instruction, the orchestrator reporting each result and what to read next, so that a run with different tooling is a different liftoff and not a different workflow.
[deterministic] The plan workflow explores the codebase and ends with a frozen plan for the human to read, cut by the task kind the liftoff names.
[deterministic] The contracts workflow builds the wave-0 seams first and halts on a spec–codebase contradiction rather than adapting around it, so that no later worker inherits a guessed seam.
[deterministic] A scout unit is built to green before the rest of its wave is dispatched, so that the implementation run can be found working before the fan-out spends anything.

[deterministic] A unit whose worker returns red or stalls gets one attempt by a stronger worker from a clean worktree holding the evidence and not the approach; a second failure stops the run naming the unit and the check that kept failing.
[deterministic] Every green unit is attacked by an adversary before it lands and lands only when no blocking finding stands, after at most one fix by its own worker.

[deterministic] After the last unit lands, verification reruns every check and a verifier tries to refute the green; then critics review the diff against the spec, fixes go back to the unit's worker, and the loop ends with no blocking finding open or at the pass cap the liftoff sets.

[deterministic] The run ends with the report and the log stub written, every worktree of the run removed with its branch kept, and a pull request opened from the run branch; merging, rejecting, deleting branches and the diagnosis are the human's.

[deterministic] The previous run's log entry reaches the next run as content in its liftoff copy, and the keys that differ from the previous run are recorded, so that a retry differs by an attributable change.

[deterministic] Checks are written by the test-builder into the run before implementation, with the map beside the spec, and are locked against the run; a check returns an exit, a ratio or a sheet and every gate reads all three.
[deterministic] A judge produces a verdict sheet against a rubric with a quotation on every answer, and an uncited sheet fails.

[deterministic] Each role's reach — tools, model, isolation, its own hooks — is declared in its own crew file and nothing it can do exceeds it; the installed settings are derived from the crew folder.
[deterministic] The explorer answers one narrow question with a cited answer and never receives the plan or a unit's work.
[deterministic] The planner turns the frozen spec, map and explorer answers into the plan and writes nothing else.
[deterministic] The orchestrator invokes workflows on the human's word, records what they return, and writes no run document itself.
[deterministic] The steward runs one leaf or git invocation for a workflow and returns its exit and output, so that workflows touch disk only through it.
[deterministic] The interface-builder writes wave-0 seams without behaviour and halts on a contradiction with the spec.
[deterministic] The implementer builds one unit in its own worktree until the unit's checks pass and cannot finish red.
[deterministic] The strong-worker retries one failed unit once on the stronger tier from a clean state.
[judged] The adversary attacks one completed unit for what its checks missed and where it narrowed scope.
[deterministic] The verifier reruns the checks on the merged branch and tries to refute the green rather than confirm it.
[judged] The critic reviews the diff against the spec and returns one finding per gap, never a fix.
[deterministic] The scribe assembles the report and the log stub from the run's records with every ledger line marked recorded, checked, reviewed or stated, and reports what it could not assemble.
[deterministic] The test-builder is a session the human starts against the frozen spec and a run, writes the map and the checks, and asks the human where the spec is silent.

[deterministic] Every subagent receives a sealed dispatch rendered from its role file, a template and the fill, committed before it is spawned, so that what is not a slot cannot reach it and a worktree sees it.
[deterministic] Every return is validated at the handoff against the role's schema by a hook that holds the agent until it validates, and is stored in the run.
[deterministic] A locked path, a frozen document, the human-owned lines of the log and the plan's boundary are refused to every tool and to the shell, and a guard that cannot decide refuses.
[deterministic] A worker cannot end its turn red: its own gate runs the unit's checks; on the fifth consecutive block it records a stall and lets the worker return so the workflow can act.
[deterministic] Every hook event is recorded in the run's event log with its source, and a session starting on a run in progress is told which launch and run it is in.
[deterministic] node flightdeck/testbench/run-all.mjs exits 0.

edges.text: the run-new script is run while the spec or map is draft, or while the previous log entry is absent or still carries a '<fill>' line: it exits 2 naming the file or the field and writes nothing; the init script on an existing name exits 1.
A frozen file is rewritten through a Bash redirect under the installed settings: the write fails and the file is unchanged; the same edit through the Edit tool is denied.
A return does not parse or fails its schema: the hook holds the agent once with the errors; on the second failure it stores the raw message as an invalid return and lets the agent go.
A worker's gate cannot find the unit's checks — no map pinned, the map unreadable, or the return names no unit: it blocks with the reason rather than passing.

flightdeck/.controlcenter/launch.yaml is absent or names a launch with no run in progress: every hook exits 0 writing nothing, except the frozen-document guard, which still refuses; every script that needs a run exits 1 naming the file.
A hook gets stdin that is not JSON, no project directory, a folder under flightdeck/launch/ without launch.json, or an event it does not record: it exits 0, prints nothing and writes nothing.

A check's command cannot spawn or exceeds 300 seconds: its verdict is error naming the cause and the remaining checks still run; a ratio below threshold is fail; a sheet missing, invalid or uncited is error.
A workflow receives args failing the liftoff schema or a draft plan, or is invoked while the run is stopped: it returns { refused: <reason> } and dispatches nothing.
A worker returns a halt (blocked, budget, boundary, unsatisfiable, test-contradicts-spec): no stronger attempt is made; the unit is carried as halted with its reason.
The pull request cannot be opened: the orchestrator reports the failure and the run branch name; the report, the log stub and the cleanup stand.
the merge script meets a red check or a conflict: it aborts, leaves branch, worktree and working tree as they were, and exits 2 naming the ids or paths.

the install script finds a target file or settings key that differs: it lists the conflicts, writes nothing and exits 2 unless --force; without --apply it prints the planned writes and writes nothing.

A tests map names a check path outside the run's checks/, flightdeck/testbench/ or launch.json.test_dir, or a ratio without trials and threshold, or a sheet without a rubric: the validate script exits 2 naming the check.
The scribe finds an input absent or unparsable: it returns what is missing and writes no report.

decisions.text: A small command surface: core scripts callable by themselves, no dispatcher and nothing that advances a run; a flight command wrapping them is deferred to a later launch, because the first attempt's runner became the system and its tests tested the runner.

Claude Code's native harness carries the conduct — agent files for roles, hooks for enforcement and recording, dynamic workflows for sequence and fan-out, the sandbox for the shell — because a mechanism the harness enforces cannot be forgotten by an agent.
Every run document is JSON with a schema and every state a human owns is a field in one, because a view layer over the files is a later launch and this one fixes what it will read.
The launch is the unit of work and the run the unit of attempt; a run has no phase field and no gate switch, because a run is the workflows invoked and what the human read between them.

Budgets belong to the workflow runtime and the agent files; the liftoff carries the sequence, the overrides and the settings, because tooling is a failure axis and a different liftoff is cheaper than a different workflow.
After the report everything is the human's — the pull request's fate, the branches, the diagnosis and the retry — because the sources put every step after the final review in the human's hands.
The spec chain and its rubric are unchanged and this launch's own run-1 is hand-made, because the first carries calibration evidence and the second predates the tools that would make it.
The two v1 attempt folders and RUNLOG.md stay as history, because no flightcrew run produced them and migrating them would edit frozen maps for nothing.

Every guard fails closed — a guard that cannot decide refuses, a recorder that cannot record stays silent — and scripts write only inside the launch, FLIGHTLOG.md and .controlcenter, because a guard that permits by failing and a script that writes anywhere were the first attempt's two silent holes; both are proven by B32 and B5.

verification.text: The test-builder writes the checks into flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-core/runs/run-1/checks/ before implementation, with the map at specs/tests-map.v1.json, and the run locks them; each is a script per C7 reusing flightdeck/testbench/fixtures and lib, and every check names the behaviours and edges it covers. Deterministic: B1, B2, E1 — run the init and run-new scripts on a temporary repository against frozen and draft fixtures and filled, unfilled and absent log entries and assert the folder, launch.json, the branch and its base, launch.yaml and the refusals. B3, E2 — an Edit envelope at a frozen fixture is denied with and without a run, and a Bash redirect under the installed settings fails. B4 — the validate script accepts every document of the sample launch and rejects mutated copies. B5, E11, E12, E13 — every core script runs by path, exits per C8, writes only where B5 allows and makes no network call, and the merge, install and validate refusals hold. B7, B8, B9, B10, B11, B12, B13, B14, E8, E9 — each workflow runs under a stub of the runtime with agent() and workflow() answered from fixtures, and the transcript and events.jsonl are asserted for the trajectory invariants: the scout's return precedes its wave, one stronger attempt then a stop naming unit and check, an adversary dispatch before every merge and at most one fix, verify then review after the last merge, the report, log stub, worktree removal and pull-request call at the end, the previous entry and the changed keys in the liftoff copy, and the refusals. B15, B16, E7 — the check script over a sample map with exit, ratio and sheet checks in passing, failing, unspawnable, below-threshold and uncited cases; a judge dispatch against a fixture rubric whose sheet validates and whose uncited sheet is refused. B17, B18, B19, B20, B21, B22, B23, B24, B26, B28, B29, E14, I10, I11, I12 — every unit's terms, operator and maintenance entries present; every crew file parsed against C2 and each role's reach; the explorer, planner, steward, interface-builder, implementer, strong-worker, verifier, scribe and test-builder each dispatched against a fixture and their returns asserted, the orchestrator against a transcript fixture, and the scribe also against a run with a missing input. B30, B31, E3 — the render script for every role asserted for line 1, slot content and the commit; return-capture with valid, invalid and repeated-invalid envelopes. B32, B33, B34, E4, E5, E6, C8 — every guard, the worker gate and event-log spawned against the sample launch with targets inside and outside the locked and allowed sets, red and green units, five consecutive blocks, no map, an unreadable record, no launch.yaml, bad stdin and an unlisted event, asserting every decision, exit and event. B35 and C1, C5, C6, C8 — the constraint checks of the testbench re-pointed at the new paths, the denyWrite superset check, the no-markdown-read check and the workflow static scan for C4. Statistical: B6 — five scripted orchestrator sessions on the sample launch with a liftoff of three entries, each passing when every workflow runs in the liftoff's order and none runs without a human turn before it, with at least four of five passing. Judged: B25, B27 — a judge sheet against a rubric under runs/run-1/checks/rubrics/ over an adversary return and a critic return on fixture diffs, verdict pass. The end-to-end proof is a real run: in a Claude Code session with the installed settings on a temporary repository holding flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-project, the human runs the init script, freezes the sample spec and map with the freeze script, runs the run-new script, pastes a library liftoff into the orchestrator and instructs each entry in turn, reading the plan and the seams between; it passes when every dispatch has a captured return, every hook event carries source hook, the report and log stub exist with the human-owned lines reading <fill>, no worktree of the run remains, a pull request or E10's failure is reported, the validate script accepts the run folder, and the run-new script refuses until the entry is filled and opens run-2 once it is. node flightdeck/testbench/run-all.mjs runs the whole set and exits 0.

acceptance.text: Every deterministic check green as exit codes, the statistical threshold of B6 met, the judged sheets of B25 and B27 passed with cited evidence, and node flightdeck/testbench/run-all.mjs exits 0. flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-core/runs/run-1/ holds its liftoff copy, plan.json, evidence/summary.json with an empty locked list, report.json and the run's dispatches and returns, all validating, and flightdeck/launch/FLIGHTLOG.md holds this run's entry with its human-owned lines reading <fill>. A critic pass over the diff against this spec returns no blocking gap, and one full transcript of the end-to-end run, chosen by the reviewer and not the producer, has been read by the human. The diff touches only flightdeck/flightcrew/**, flightdeck/launch/README.md, flightdeck/launch/FLIGHTLOG.md, flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-core/**, flightdeck/.controlcenter/, flightdeck/testbench/**, flightdeck/manuals/launch/**, flightdeck/manuals/harness/**, flightdeck/manuals/orchestration/**, flightdeck/manuals/testing/**, flightdeck/manuals/README.md, flightdeck/manuals/operators-manual.md, flightdeck/manuals/maintenance-manual.md, library/terms.md, .claude/workflows/**, .claude/agents/**, .claude/settings.json, .gitignore and CLAUDE.md.
